# Python idiom

Match `pyproject.toml`, lockfiles, supported interpreters, CI, formatter/linter, type checker, and test
framework before selecting syntax or tools.

## Runtime and tooling

- Version-gate behavior: `TaskGroup`/`ExceptionGroup` require 3.11; `typing.override` requires 3.12;
  free-threaded CPython is experimental from 3.13; deferred annotation evaluation changes in 3.14.
  Use backports only when the repository already supports them.
- Imports must not connect to services, start threads, parse CLI arguments, or mutate runtime config.
  Put startup behind a function and scripts behind `if __name__ == "__main__"`.
- Add precise annotations where they protect a public or complex boundary; do not add ceremony to
  obvious local code. Narrow `Any`/`object` at the boundary and remember annotations are not runtime
  validation.
- Match the repository's environment manager and lockfile. When none exists, `uv` is a supported
  option for environments, locking/sync, execution, tools, and pip-compatible workflows; once
  selected, do not mix managers or lockfiles. Never install into the system interpreter.
- Use the repository's formatter/linter. Ruff may own linting and formatting; keep preview behavior
  out of CI unless explicitly accepted and pinned.

## Correctness

- Avoid mutable defaults; use `is None` when absence differs from falsiness; close files, locks,
  clients, and connections with context managers.
- Catch the narrow exception you can handle. At a boundary, translate or re-raise with context
  (`raise DomainError(...) from exc`); never silently continue after `except Exception`.
- Use timezone-aware instants, explicit decimal/money rules, and deliberate closure binding. Do not
  mutate a collection while iterating or assume a generator can be consumed twice.
- In async code, keep blocking work off the event loop, own every created task, and re-raise
  cancellation after cleanup.

## Operational safety

- Use `subprocess.run([...], check=True)` with an argument list. Avoid `shell=True`; if the shell is
  required, untrusted values never enter the command text.
- Give network calls finite timeouts, check response status, and retry only safe transient work with
  bounded backoff. Parameterize SQL and never deserialize untrusted pickle data.
- Generate credentials/tokens with `secrets`, redact logs, and separate decision from effect so dry
  run and approval boundaries are testable.

## Tests

Match the repository's framework. With pytest, use parametrization/fixtures and boundary fakes where
they improve behavior tests; inject clocks rather than sleeping. `pytest --cov` is provided by the
`pytest-cov` plugin, not pytest core. Run the regression-first process in [tests first](./tdd.md) and
report meaningful untested behavior rather than chasing a coverage number.
